decision.chosen: Add a [[tool.mypy.overrides]] block to pyproject.toml for module = ["langgraph.*", "opentelemetry.*"] with follow_imports = "skip" and ignore_errors = true.

Under that flag mypy cannot resolve the package and reports attr-defined. Verified fix: with the override added, graph.py:35, graph_builder.py:28 and a2a_protocol.py:26 all report 0 attr-defined errors. This is the same toolchain-crash class already handled for numpy/torch/transformers/websockets/uvicorn at pyproject.toml:209-212, so it follows existing house precedent.

decision.chosen: config/__init__.py:20 and core/__init__.py:42 get `-> ModuleType` (add `from types import ModuleType`). core/orchestrator/__init__.py:83 gets `-> Any` (add `from typing import Any`).
decision.reason: The first two return `import_module(...)`, which is a module, on every returning branch. The third returns the DAGOrchestrator CLASS, and naming its type would require a module-level import of beagle.core.autonomous_orchestrator — which is the exact circular import the lazy __getattr__ exists to break. Any is the honest type there, not a guess.
decision.rejected: Loses real type information at two of the three sites.

decision.chosen: Annotate as bare `np.ndarray`, except turboquant.py:360 which gets `Any`.
decision.reason: House precedent is bare np.ndarray — see context/embedding_cache.py:76 `arr: np.ndarray = np.load(file_path)` and :131 `results: dict[int, np.ndarray]`. turboquant.py:360 is `total = counts.sum()`, a numpy scalar rather than an array, and numpy resolves to Any under the existing override, so Any is the accurate type. Do not cast with int() — that changes runtime behaviour.
decision.rejected: Not used anywhere in this repo; introducing a second convention makes the codebase inconsistent.

decision.chosen: Underscore-prefix the parameter at all five sites. Do not add entries to .vulture_whitelist.py.
decision.reason: All five are parameters required by a contract but unused in the body, which is exactly the case .vulture_whitelist.py's own header documents as "Fixed by prefixing with underscore". Renaming is safe at every site because every caller passes positionally: build_workflow_graph is called positionally at workflow_builder.py:317 and workflow_loader.py:303; _create_chunks_from_boundaries has one caller, context_preprocessor.py:189, positional; __missing__ and __new__ are dunders invoked by the interpreter. graph_builder.py:345 already carries `_workflow_query` in the very same signature, so the rename matches the file's local convention.
decision.rejected: The whitelist is for fixtures, re-exports and probes. Using it for an ordinary unused parameter suppresses the finding instead of fixing the input.
Every one is required by its caller or by the interpreter's dunder contract. Deleting changes the signature and breaks the call.

decision.chosen: Declare `_singleton_instance: ClassVar[Any]` in the class body of `class Singleton[T](ABC)` at state.py:298, directly after its docstring.
decision.reason: get_instance assigns cls._singleton_instance at state.py:342 and reads it at :343, but the attribute is never declared, so mypy reports attr-defined twice. ClassVar cannot contain a type variable, so ClassVar[Singleton[T]] is rejected by mypy; ClassVar[Any] is the only form that types a per-subclass class attribute here. NOTE: this defect was INTRODUCED by the previous plan's own E-04 remediation, whose verify gate was ruff-only and therefore could not see it.
decision.rejected: mypy rejects a type variable inside ClassVar.

decision.chosen: Annotate `read_stream(stream: asyncio.StreamReader, target_list: list[str], stream_type: str) -> None`, AND guard the call sites at :638-639 because process.stdout / process.stderr are typed `StreamReader | None`.
decision.reason: Annotating alone converts a no-untyped-def finding into two arg-type findings, because asyncio.subprocess.Process.stdout is Optional. The complete fix is both edits together. stream_type is genuinely used, at :633.
decision.rejected: Would force a None check inside the loop body and change the function's contract; the guard belongs at the call site where the Process object is known.
